_comment: Synthetic administrative emails for Northbridge Health Network. 'restricted' sensitivity items are visible only to personas listed in acl (drives the permission-trimming governance demo). The Lumina vendor go-live thread (EML-001/002) is visible to the external vendor persona; the leadership commercial-penalty thread (EML-003/004) is restricted to operations leadership + quality PM. Internal corrective-action threads are staff-only (not the vendor). NO PHI.

emails.subject: Westgate go-live readiness — Lumina status and date
emails.body: Robert — Lumina's view on the Westgate go-live: the build is configured and our trainers have completed ~80% of end-user sessions. We are holding the 22-JUN target. The one remaining item on our side is your team's sign-off on the medication-list data migration validation. Can you confirm (1) the migration validation will be complete by 13-JUN and (2) training sign-off so we can issue a written go-live confirmation? — Tom, Lumina Health Systems.

emails.subject: RE: Westgate go-live readiness — Lumina status and date
emails.body: Tom — thanks. We are asking Lumina to confirm in writing: (1) the medication-list data migration validation is complete and signed off, and (2) the final go-live date of 22-JUN. On our side Greg Sullivan owns the migration validation, due 13-JUN. Once both are confirmed we will issue the go-live notice to Westgate staff.

emails.subject: CONFIDENTIAL: Lumina contract — service-credit clause if Westgate slips
emails.body: Maria — leadership-only. If Westgate go-live slips past 22-JUN due to Lumina-side delays, our MSA clause 7.4 entitles us to a service credit of 8% of the implementation fee per week of delay. Do not raise this with the vendor yet; I want it in our back pocket for the readiness-review escalation if the migration validation slips. Keep this off the committee channels.

emails.subject: RE: CONFIDENTIAL: Lumina contract — service-credit clause if Westgate slips
emails.body: Understood, James — I'll keep the commercial terms out of the committee notes. I'll flag to you privately if the 13-JUN migration validation looks like it will miss.

emails.subject: Open corrective actions — why CAPA-001 and CAPA-004 are stalled
emails.body: Maria — status on our two open quality corrective actions: CAPA-001 (medication-reconciliation policy finalisation) is past due — I have the draft but I'm waiting on David Munoz's updated workflow steps before compliance review can start. CAPA-004 (Westgate environment-of-care documentation) is also past due — Priya is blocked waiting on a facilities vendor quote for the signage update. Both are on the readiness-review critical path; flagging so we can unblock before Joint Commission.

emails.subject: Provider-onboarding gap (CAPA-002) closed
emails.body: Maria — confirming for the readiness review: the Credentialing Committee closed the provider-onboarding gap on 05-JUN. The primary-source verification backlog is cleared and the onboarding checklist updated (CAPA-002 is Closed). This was the credentialing item the Quality Steering Committee flagged as related to the medication-reconciliation readiness work.

emails.subject: Biomedical equipment calibration schedule — Westgate & Riverside
emails.body: Karen — MediTech update on the biomedical calibration schedule: Riverside clinic defibrillator and infusion-pump calibrations are complete. Westgate has two outstanding items: (1) the patient-monitor bank (12 units) calibration is scheduled for 14-JUL, and (2) the autoclave validation is due 18-JUL. Both must be done before the Joint Commission survey window. We need your facilities team to confirm equipment access for those dates. — Rachel, MediTech Biomedical.

emails.subject: RE: Biomedical equipment calibration schedule — Westgate & Riverside
emails.body: Rachel — thanks. I've confirmed access for 14-JUL (patient monitors) and 18-JUL (autoclave). Please issue calibration certificates within 48 hours of completion — we need them filed before the Joint Commission survey. Copying Priya Raman from Compliance. — Karen, VMO.

emails.subject: Delivery delay — controlled-substance audit log binders
emails.body: Karen — flagging a supply-chain delay: the pre-printed controlled-substance audit log binders for Westgate pharmacy are delayed by our print vendor. Original delivery was 11-JUL; revised ETA is 16-JUL. This should not affect your monthly pharmacy audit cycle (due 25-JUL), but I wanted to flag it early. All other Q3 supply shipments (formulary kits, PPE restocks) are on schedule. — Steve, PharmaLink Distributors.

emails.subject: RE: Delivery delay — controlled-substance audit log binders
emails.body: Steve — understood on the 16-JUL revised ETA. Our pharmacy coordinator David Munoz needs these for the controlled-substance reconciliation ahead of Joint Commission. If 16-JUL slips further, our SLA clause 5.2 allows a 5% credit on the delayed line item per week of delay. Please treat this as priority. — Karen, VMO.

emails.subject: ClearPoint CPOE upgrade — v4.2 patch and Westgate lab interface
emails.body: Karen — ClearPoint status on the CPOE upgrade: the v4.2 patch (medication-interaction alerting enhancement) is code-complete and in our QA. We are targeting deployment to your staging environment by 17-JUL with production cutover on 21-JUL. The Westgate lab-order interface is tested and ready — waiting on your IT team to open the HL7 feed from LuminaEHR. Can Robert Klein coordinate the interface activation? — Lisa, ClearPoint Clinical Solutions.

emails.subject: RE: ClearPoint CPOE upgrade — v4.2 patch and Westgate lab interface
emails.body: Lisa — confirmed. Robert Klein will coordinate the HL7 feed activation with Lumina by 15-JUL so it's ready for your 17-JUL staging deployment. The 21-JUL production cutover works for us — it aligns with the post-go-live stabilisation window. Please confirm the v4.2 patch includes the Joint Commission medication-management alerting requirements per Appendix C of our agreement. — Karen, VMO.

emails.subject: Weekly vendor status roll-up — week of 07-JUL
emails.body:
James — weekly vendor roll-up:

1. Lumina Health Systems (EHR): Westgate go-live completed 22-JUN on schedule. Post-go-live support period runs through 22-JUL. No open SLA issues.
2. MediTech Biomedical (Equipment): Two calibration items outstanding at Westgate — patient monitors (14-JUL) and autoclave (18-JUL). On track.
3. PharmaLink Distributors (Supplies): Controlled-substance audit log binders delayed to 16-JUL (was 11-JUL). SLA credit clause in play if it slips further. All other deliveries on schedule.
4. ClearPoint Clinical Solutions (Software): CPOE v4.2 patch targeting 17-JUL staging, 21-JUL production. Waiting on HL7 feed activation from Lumina.

Overall: 1 minor delay (PharmaLink), 0 SLA breaches this week. Joint Commission readiness items on track.

emails.subject: CONFIDENTIAL: Vendor contract renewal calendar — Q3 actions
emails.body:
Karen — heads-up on upcoming renewals:

1. MediTech Biomedical MSA renews 01-SEP — auto-renewal unless 60-day notice. Performance has been solid; recommend renewal with updated calibration SLA (reduce response from 48h to 24h).
2. PharmaLink distribution agreement renews 15-OCT — this is the one with the supply-delay issues. Marcus recommends rebidding the controlled-substance segment while keeping the formulary-kit line.
3. ClearPoint license renewal is not until 01-MAR-2027 — no action now but flag the v4.2 upgrade performance for the renewal negotiation.

None of these are urgent but all should be on the leadership radar for Q3 planning.
